cfs.subject: member resolution order
cfs.statement: **Member resolution order (CF-ETS-001).** Looking up member *name* on a value `v` (wrapped as a `PSObject`) proceeds in this order and returns the first hit: (1) the reserved names `psbase`, `psadapted`, `psextended`, `psobject` and `pstypenames`, generated on demand; (2) **instance members** added to this object (for example by `Add-Member`); (3) **type-table (extended) members** merged over the object's type-name hierarchy, most specific type name winning; (4) **adapted members** from the adapter chosen for the object; (5) **base members**: the .NET members of the wrapped object, only when the chosen adapter is not already the .NET adapter. Member-name matching in the .NET adapter is case-insensitive (its binding flags include `IgnoreCase`). Type-table collection entries are marked "replicate and clone when returning" (a copy bound to the current object is handed out), adapted and base entries are not; the enumeration order across sources is `UNVERIFIED` (VB-038). Member lookup on a `PSMemberSet` owner searches the set's own members first, then the same collections.
cfs.label: FACT-SRC

deviations.baseline_behavior: Adapters exist for WMI, DirectoryEntry, DataRow/DataRowView, COM, CIM and XML nodes.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Ship .NET, XML, PSObject, member-set and the third-party adapter bridge only.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Scripts using those object kinds lose adapted members.

deviations.baseline_behavior: Built-in type data is compiled into C# from types.ps1xml.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Compile at build time and also publish a versioned data file.
deviations.benefit: One source for tooling and a clean-room implementation.
